editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Sports Club Activity That PMA Cannot Register in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Other Sports Clubs can be fully foreign-owned nationally, yet Bali’s scale structure closes the registration path to a PT PMA.
editorial.body:
**A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today.** That is the practical starting point for Other Sports Clubs, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign investment with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. The contrast is not a minor footnote: nationally, full foreign ownership is permitted; in Bali, the available registration structure prevents a PT PMA from taking this activity forward. Reading only the national opening would miss the operational result on the island.

The activity covers professional, semi-professional and amateur sports clubs that give members an opportunity to participate in sport, whether or not the club provides a venue and facilities. Its centre of gravity is the club as an organised membership setting for participation, rather than a definition tied to owning a particular site. The scope expressly includes winter-sports clubs, chess clubs, athletics clubs for running, jumping and throwing, shooting clubs, e-sports clubs, and card-game clubs such as trump or bridge. The examples are varied, but the common thread is clear: members are given a route into sporting activity.

Registration is open at the Mikro, Kecil and Menengah scales. That detail becomes decisive in Bali because OSS has no Usaha Besar scale row for this activity. Bali’s record therefore treats it as reserved for UMKM on structural grounds. A PT PMA is, by law, an Usaha Besar, and it consequently cannot register this activity there. This does not alter the national description of the club activity itself; it determines who can use the registration path in Bali.

The record also notes Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA block for low- and medium-low-risk activities, under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. For this activity, the stated conclusion remains direct: Bali is closed to PMA because no Usaha Besar scale is available. Nationally, it is TERBUKA and may carry foreign ownership up to 100%; in Bali, a foreign investor cannot register it through a PT PMA. The national ceiling describes foreign-ownership capacity, but it does not override Bali’s recorded registration position.
